headline: US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid escalating Houthi attacks on civilian targets
summary: The order follows recent attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis on civilian targets in Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil fields, escalating regional conflict.
details: The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and their family members to depart from its missions in Saudi Arabia. This decision comes amidst a series of attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis on civilian targets within the country.

Recent attacks include one at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, which killed one person and injured eight others. Additionally, two people were killed in a drone attack on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield.

State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott confirmed the order, stating it applies to "non-emergency US government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only." He highlighted increased Houthi hostilities against Saudi Arabia, targeting critical infrastructure and causing civilian casualties.

This latest withdrawal follows a period where some diplomatic personnel had returned to the region after earlier Iranian attacks on US facilities. The current escalation is linked to the wider regional conflict triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Four US officials also indicated that family members would be ordered to leave US missions in other Gulf states, though Pigott did not address this publicly. The US embassy in Riyadh had previously issued a security alert regarding potential further Houthi attacks.

headline: Seven more die of dengue, 1,373 hospitalised across Bangladesh
summary: Bangladesh reports a significant rise in dengue cases and fatalities. All seven new deaths occurred in Dhaka South City Corporation, bringing the year's total to 364.
details: Seven more people have died from dengue, and 1,373 new patients were hospitalized across Bangladesh in the 24 hours leading up to yesterday morning. This data was released by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
All seven recent fatalities were reported within the Dhaka South City Corporation area. The total death toll from dengue this year has now climbed to 364.
The cumulative number of dengue cases recorded this year has reached 116,990. Currently, 5,970 dengue patients are receiving treatment in various hospitals nationwide.
